   161→    <prerequisite ref="build">All gates passed (lint, test, build)</prerequisite>
   162→    <instructions>
   163→      <instruction>
   164→        Stage Selectively: Add only the files related to this change.
   165→        <command>git add [specific files]</command>
   166→        <anti-pattern>git add -A (may include unrelated changes)</anti-pattern>
   167→      </instruction>
   168→      <instruction>
   169→        Write the Message: Explain WHY, not just WHAT.
   170→        <format>
   171→          <line>Short description in imperative mood, 50 chars or less</line>
   172→          <line></line>
   173→          <line>Longer explanation of why this change was made,</line>
   174→          <line>what problem it solves, and any important context.</line>
   175→          <line>Wrap at 72 characters.</line>
   176→        </format>
   177→        <rules>
   178→          <rule>Imperative mood ("Add feature" not "Added feature")</rule>
   179→          <rule>Capitalize first letter, no period at end</rule>
   180→          <rule>No type prefixes (no "feat:", "fix:", etc.)</rule>
   181→        </rules>
   182→      </instruction>
   183→      <instruction>
   184→        Verify Atomicity: This commit should be independently checkable, buildable, testable, and documented.
   185→      </instruction>
   186→    </instructions>
   187→    <gate>
   188→      <condition>Commit contains code + tests + docs for one logical change</condition>
   189→      <on_fail>Split into smaller commits or add missing pieces</on_fail>
   190→    </gate>
   191→  </step>
   192→
   193→  <step number="8" id="post-commit">
   194→    <title>Post-Commit Verification</title>
   195→    <goal>Confirm the commit didn't break anything.</goal>
   196→    <prerequisite ref="commit">Commit created</prerequisite>
   197→    <!-- Optimization: no source code changes between build step and here (only git add/commit).
   198→         A lightweight cargo check confirms compilation still holds post-commit. -->
   199→    <instructions>
   200→      <instruction>
   201→        <command>cargo check --all-features</command>
   202→        <expected>Committed state compiles cleanly</expected>
   203→      </instruction>
   204→      <instruction>
   205→        <command>git log -1 --stat</command>
   206→        <rationale>Review what was actually committed</rationale>
   207→      </instruction>
   208→    </instructions>
   209→  </step>
   210→
   211→  <step number="9" id="transition">
   212→    <title>Transition</title>
   213→    <goal>Clean context switch to next task.</goal>
   214→    <instructions>
   215→      <instruction>
   216→        Clean Slate: Clear your mental context. The previous task is done.
   217→      </instruction>
   218→      <instruction goto="specification">
   219→        Next Task: Pick the next item from your backlog and return to specification.
   220→      </instruction>
   221→    </instructions>
   222→  </step>
   223→</steps>
   224→
   225→<verification-commands>
   226→  <description>Quick reference for all verification commands in order (matches CI):</description>
   227→  <command-sequence>
   228→    <command>cargo doc --no-deps --all-features</command>
   229→    <command>cargo fmt -- --check</command>
   230→    <command>cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings</command>
   231→    <command note="NO FILTERS - run entire suite with all features">cargo test --all-features</command>
   232→    <command>cargo check --all-targets --all-features</command>
   233→    <command>cargo build --release</command>
   234→    <command>cargo llvm-cov --all-features --fail-under-lines 90</command>
   235→  </command-sequence>
   236→  <critical>
   237→    `cargo test --all-features` must be run WITHOUT name filters. Never filter tests.
   238→    Output must show "0 filtered out" - any other number is wrong.
   239→    All flags (--all-targets, --all-features) match CI exactly.
   240→  </critical>
   241→</verification-commands>
   242→
   243→<principles>
   244→  <principle name="Atomic">Each commit is complete and independent</principle>
   245→  <principle name="Test-First">Tests define behavior before implementation</principle>
   246→  <principle name="Zero-Warning">Warnings are errors; fix them immediately</principle>
   247→  <principle name="Document-As-You-Go">Docs are part of the deliverable, not an afterthought</principle>
   248→  <principle name="Small-Steps">Prefer many small commits over few large ones</principle>
   249→</principles>

   226→  let cli = Cli::parse();
   227→
   228→  // CORRECT - explicit args, works in tests
   229→  let cli = Cli::parse_from(["bivvy", "run", "--verbose"]);

   235→  - Any test that needs to verify CLI behavior

   243→  PREFER runnable examples with real test fixtures:
   244→  ```rust
   245→  /// ```
   246→  /// use bivvy::config::load_merged_config;
   247→  /// use tempfile::TempDir;
   248→  /// use std::fs;
   249→  ///
   250→  /// // Create real test files
   251→  /// let temp = TempDir::new().unwrap();
   252→  /// fs::create_dir_all(temp.path().join(".bivvy")).unwrap();
   253→  /// fs::write(temp.path().join(".bivvy/config.yml"), "app_name: test").unwrap();
   254→  ///
   255→  /// // Test with real data
   256→  /// let config = load_merged_config(temp.path()).unwrap();
   257→  /// assert_eq!(config.app_name, Some("test".to_string()));
   258→  /// ```
   259→  ```
   260→
   261→  Use `no_run` ONLY for code that truly can't run in tests (interactive terminal
   262→  input, network calls to real servers, etc.):
   263→  ```rust
   264→  /// ```no_run
   265→  /// // Requires interactive terminal input
   266→  /// let answer = ui.prompt_confirm("Continue?")?;
   267→  /// ```
   268→  ```
   269→
   270→  Use `ignore` only for pseudocode that won't compile. Always explain why:

   272→  /// ```ignore
   273→  /// // Pseudocode showing concept - yaml() helper doesn't exist
   274→  /// let config = yaml("key: value");
   275→  /// ```
   276→  ```

1→# Configuration
     2→
     3→Bivvy uses YAML configuration files to define your project setup.
     4→
     5→## File Locations
     6→
     7→Configuration is loaded and merged in this order (later overrides earlier):
     8→
     9→1. Remote base configs (from `extends:`)
    10→2. User global config (`~/.bivvy/config.yml`)
    11→3. Project config (`.bivvy/config.yml`)
    12→4. Local overrides (`.bivvy/config.local.yml`) - gitignored
    13→
    14→## Basic Structure
    15→
    16→```yaml
    17→app_name: "MyApp"
    18→
    19→settings:
    20→  default_output: verbose  # verbose | quiet | silent
    21→
    22→steps:
    23→  install_deps:
    24→    command: "npm install"
    25→
    26→workflows:
    27→  default:
    28→    steps: [install_deps]
    29→```
    30→
    31→## Variable Interpolation
    32→
    33→Use `${VAR}` syntax to interpolate values:
    34→
    35→```yaml
    36→steps:
    37→  setup:
    38→    command: "echo Setting up ${project_name}"
    39→```
    40→
    41→### Built-in Variables
    42→
    43→| Variable | Description |
    44→|----------|-------------|
    45→| `${project_name}` | Directory name of the project |
    46→| `${project_root}` | Absolute path to project root |
    47→
    48→### Environment Variables
    49→
    50→Environment variables are available for interpolation:
    51→
    52→```yaml
    53→steps:
    54→  deploy:
    55→    command: "deploy --env ${RAILS_ENV}"
    56→```
    57→
    58→### Escaping
    59→
    60→Use `$${` to escape (outputs literal `${`):
    61→
    62→```yaml
    63→steps:
    64→  example:
    65→    command: "echo '$${NOT_INTERPOLATED}'"  # outputs: ${NOT_INTERPOLATED}
    66→```
    67→
    68→## Deep Merge Behavior
    69→
    70→When multiple config files define the same key:
    71→
    72→- **Objects**: Recursively merged (nested keys combined)
    73→- **Arrays**: Replaced entirely (not concatenated)
    74→- **Scalars**: Later value wins
    75→
    76→```yaml
    77→# .bivvy/config.yml
    78→steps:
    79→  deps:
    80→    command: "yarn install"
    81→    env:
    82→      NODE_ENV: development
    83→
    84→# .bivvy/config.local.yml
    85→steps:
    86→  deps:
    87→    env:
    88→      NODE_ENV: production
    89→      # command is preserved from base
    90→```
    91→

    93→
    94→- [Steps Configuration](steps.md)
    95→- [Workflows Configuration](workflows.md)
    96→- [Completed Checks](completed-checks.md)

Now I have a thorough understanding of the codebase. Let me present the complete implementation plan.

---

## Implementation Plan: TOML Configuration Support for Bivvy

### 1. Overall Strategy: Option A -- Convert TOML to `serde_yaml::Value`

After examining the entire config pipeline, **Option A** is the right choice. Here is the rationale:

- The merger (`src/config/merger.rs`) operates entirely on `serde_yaml::Value`. Changing it to `serde_json::Value` (Option B) would require modifying the merger, the extends resolver, and every call site -- a large, risky refactor touching 5+ files.
- Option C (struct-level merging) loses critical merge semantics like "null deletes key."
- Option A requires adding a single conversion function (`toml::Value` to `serde_yaml::Value`) and adjusting file discovery. The merger, extends resolver, and all downstream consumers remain untouched.

The `toml::Value` to `serde_yaml::Value` conversion is straightforward because both are recursive enum types mapping to the same JSON-like data model: strings, integers, floats, booleans, arrays, and tables/mappings. The one edge case is that TOML distinguishes between `Integer` and `Float` while `serde_yaml::Value` uses `Number`, but both map naturally.

### 2. New Dependency

Add to `Cargo.toml` under `[dependencies]`:

```toml
toml = "0.8"
```

The `toml` crate version 0.8 is the current stable release. It provides `toml::Value` and `toml::from_str` for parsing.

### 3. Configuration Format Enum

Create a new enum in `src/config/loader.rs` to represent the detected format:

```rust
/// Configuration file format.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ConfigFormat {
    Yaml,
    Toml,
}
```

This will be stored in `ConfigPaths` so that all downstream code knows which format the project uses without re-detecting.

### 4. File Discovery Changes (`src/config/loader.rs`)

#### 4a. `ConfigPaths` struct modification

Add a `format` field:

```rust
pub struct ConfigPaths {
    pub extends: Vec<PathBuf>,
    pub user_global: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub project: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub project_local: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// The detected config format for this project.
    pub format: ConfigFormat,
}
```

#### 4b. Discovery logic

Each of the three `find_*` methods needs to check for both extensions. The file priority within a single location should be:

1. YAML first (`.yml`), since it is the existing default
2. TOML second (`.toml`)

But the critical constraint is: **all files in the merge chain must use the same format**. The discovery algorithm:

1. `find_project_config(project_root)` -- check for `.bivvy/config.yml` first, then `.bivvy/config.toml`. Whichever exists determines the project format. If both exist, return an error (see 4c).
2. Once the project format is known, `find_user_global()` looks for `~/.bivvy/config.yml` or `~/.bivvy/config.toml` based on the detected format.
3. `find_project_local(project_root)` looks for `.bivvy/config.local.yml` or `.bivvy/config.local.toml` based on the detected format.

The updated `discover` method becomes:

```rust
impl ConfigPaths {
    pub fn discover(project_root: &Path) -> std::result::Result<Self, BivvyError> {
        let (project, format) = Self::find_project_config(project_root)?;
        Ok(Self {
            extends: Vec::new(),
            user_global: Self::find_user_global(format),
            project,
            project_local: Self::find_project_local(project_root, format),
            format,
        })
    }
}
```

Note: `discover` currently returns `Self` (infallible). It must now return `Result<Self, BivvyError>` because it can fail if both formats exist. This is a breaking signature change. All callers of `ConfigPaths::discover()` must handle the Result.

#### 4c. Conflict detection

If both `.bivvy/config.yml` and `.bivvy/config.toml` exist, return a new error variant:

```rust
BivvyError::ConfigFormatConflict {
    path: PathBuf,  // the .bivvy directory
    message: String, // "Both config.yml and config.toml exist. Remove one."
}
```

This is added to `src/error.rs`.

#### 4d. Extension helper

Add a helper to get the file extension for a format:

```rust
impl ConfigFormat {
    pub fn extension(&self) -> &str {
        match self {
            ConfigFormat::Yaml => "yml",
            ConfigFormat::Toml => "toml",
        }
    }
    
    pub fn local_filename(&self) -> &str {
        match self {
            ConfigFormat::Yaml => "config.local.yml",
            ConfigFormat::Toml => "config.local.toml",
        }
    }
    
    pub fn config_filename(&self) -> &str {
        match self {
            ConfigFormat::Yaml => "config.yml",
            ConfigFormat::Toml => "config.toml",
        }
    }
}
```

### 5. TOML-to-YAML Value Conversion (`src/config/loader.rs`)

Add a conversion function:

```rust
/// Convert a toml::Value into serde_yaml::Value so it can be fed
/// into the existing merger pipeline unchanged.
fn toml_to_yaml_value(toml_val: &toml::Value) -> serde_yaml::Value {
    match toml_val {
        toml::Value::String(s) => serde_yaml::Value::String(s.clone()),
        toml::Value::Integer(i) => serde_yaml::Value::Number(serde_yaml::Number::from(*i)),
        toml::Value::Float(f) => {
            // serde_yaml::Number::from only takes i64/u64/f64
            serde_yaml::Value::Number(serde_yaml::Number::from(*f))
        }
        toml::Value::Boolean(b) => serde_yaml::Value::Bool(*b),
        toml::Value::Datetime(dt) => {
            // TOML datetimes have no direct YAML equivalent; store as string
            serde_yaml::Value::String(dt.to_string())
        }
        toml::Value::Array(arr) => {
            serde_yaml::Value::Sequence(arr.iter().map(toml_to_yaml_value).collect())
        }
        toml::Value::Table(table) => {
            let mut mapping = serde_yaml::Mapping::new();
            for (k, v) in table {
                mapping.insert(
                    serde_yaml::Value::String(k.clone()),
                    toml_to_yaml_value(v),
                );
            }
            serde_yaml::Value::Mapping(mapping)
        }
    }
}
```

This is about 25 lines of pure, easily-testable transformation code.

### 6. Loading Functions (`src/config/loader.rs`)

#### 6a. `load_config_value` -- format-aware

The current `load_config_value` always parses as YAML. It needs to accept a format parameter or detect format from the file extension:

```rust
/// Load a config file as raw serde_yaml::Value (for merging).
///
/// Detects format from the file extension (.toml vs .yml/.yaml).
pub fn load_config_value(path: &Path) -> Result<serde_yaml::Value> {
    let content = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| /* same as today */)?;
    
    let format = detect_format_from_path(path);
    match format {
        ConfigFormat::Toml => {
            let toml_val: toml::Value = toml::from_str(&content)
                .map_err(|e| BivvyError::ConfigParseError {
                    path: path.to_path_buf(),
                    message: e.to_string(),
                })?;
            Ok(toml_to_yaml_value(&toml_val))
        }
        ConfigFormat::Yaml => {
            serde_yaml::from_str(&content).map_err(|e| BivvyError::ConfigParseError {
                path: path.to_path_buf(),
                message: e.to_string(),
            })
        }
    }
}

fn detect_format_from_path(path: &Path) -> ConfigFormat {
    match path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) {
        Some("toml") => ConfigFormat::Toml,
        _ => ConfigFormat::Yaml,
    }
}
```

#### 6b. `parse_config` and `load_config_file` -- format-aware

Similarly, `parse_config` needs a TOML branch:

```rust
pub fn parse_config(content: &str, source_path: &Path) -> Result<BivvyConfig> {
    let format = detect_format_from_path(source_path);
    match format {
        ConfigFormat::Toml => {
            toml::from_str(content).map_err(|e| BivvyError::ConfigParseError {
                path: source_path.to_path_buf(),
                message: e.to_string(),
            })
        }
        ConfigFormat::Yaml => {
            serde_yaml::from_str(content).map_err(|e| BivvyError::ConfigParseError {
                path: source_path.to_path_buf(),
                message: e.to_string(),
            })
        }
    }
}
```

This works because `BivvyConfig` already derives `Serialize, Deserialize` from serde, which is format-agnostic. Both `toml::from_str` and `serde_yaml::from_str` use serde's deserialization framework.

#### 6c. `load_merged_config` error path update

When no project config is found, the error message currently hardcodes `config.yml`:

```rust
return Err(BivvyError::ConfigNotFound {
    path: project_root.join(".bivvy").join("config.yml"),
});
```

This should say something like `config.yml (or config.toml)` since neither format was found. One approach: change the message to reference the `.bivvy` directory rather than a specific file, or mention both file names.

#### 6d. `load_merged_config` -- handle `discover` returning `Result`

The call `ConfigPaths::discover(project_root)` now returns a `Result`. All callers need the `?` operator:

```rust
let paths = ConfigPaths::discover(project_root)?;
```

### 7. Init Command Changes (`src/cli/commands/init.rs`)

#### 7a. New `--format` flag on `InitArgs`

Add to `src/cli/args.rs`:

```rust
pub struct InitArgs {
    // ... existing fields ...
    
    /// Config format to generate: yaml or toml
    #[arg(long, default_value = "yaml")]
    pub format: String,
}
```

#### 7b. Format-aware config generation

The `create_config` method in `InitCommand` currently generates YAML strings manually. For TOML, we need a parallel path. There are two approaches:

**Approach 1 (Recommended):** Keep the existing YAML string builder for YAML, and add a `create_config_toml` method that builds a TOML string. The TOML output would look like:

```toml
# Bivvy configuration for MyApp

app_name = "MyApp"

[settings]
default_output = "verbose"  # verbose | quiet | silent

[steps.bundler]
template = "bundler"
# command = "bundle install"

[workflows.default]
steps = ["bundler"]
```

**Approach 2:** Serialize from `BivvyConfig` struct. Build a `BivvyConfig` programmatically and call `toml::to_string_pretty(&config)`. The downside is losing the nice commented-out hints and explanatory comments.

I recommend Approach 1 because the init output is heavily commented and formatted for human readability -- this is not a purely mechanical serialization task.

#### 7c. File writing

Change the write path to be format-aware:

```rust
let filename = match self.args.format.as_str() {
    "toml" => "config.toml",
    _ => "config.yml",
};
fs::write(bivvy_dir.join(filename), &config)?;
```

#### 7d. Gitignore update

The `update_gitignore` method currently adds `.bivvy/config.local.yml`. It should add the correct local filename based on the format:

```rust
let gitignore_entry = match self.args.format.as_str() {
    "toml" => ".bivvy/config.local.toml",
    _ => ".bivvy/config.local.yml",
};
```

#### 7e. `config_exists` check

Currently checks only for `config.yml`. Update to check both:

```rust
fn config_exists(&self) -> bool {
    self.project_root.join(".bivvy/config.yml").exists()
        || self.project_root.join(".bivvy/config.toml").exists()
}
```

### 8. Error Type Changes (`src/error.rs`)

Add one new variant:

```rust
/// Both YAML and TOML config files found in the same location.
#[error("Config format conflict in {path}: {message}")]
ConfigFormatConflict { path: PathBuf, message: String },
```

### 9. Config Module Exports (`src/config/mod.rs`)

Add the new `ConfigFormat` type to the public re-exports:

```rust
pub use loader::{
    find_project_root, load_config, load_config_file, load_config_value,
    load_merged_config, load_merged_config_with_resolver, parse_config,
    ConfigFormat, ConfigPaths,
};
```

### 10. Callers of `ConfigPaths::discover` That Need Updating

Since `discover` now returns `Result`, every call site must be updated. Based on grep results, these are:

| File | Current usage |
|------|---------------|
| `src/config/loader.rs` (`load_merged_config_with_resolver`) | `ConfigPaths::discover(project_root)` |
| `src/cli/commands/lint.rs` | `ConfigPaths::discover(&self.project_root)` |

| `src/cli/commands/status.rs` | `ConfigPaths::discover(...)` |
| `src/cli/commands/run.rs` | `ConfigPaths::discover(...)` (if applicable) |

Each needs `?` appended or `.unwrap_or_else(...)` handling. The lint and config commands would surface the error to the user.

**Alternative:** Keep `discover` infallible and add a separate `discover_strict` that returns `Result`, or have `discover` return `Self` but store a `conflict: bool` field that callers can check. ### 11. Extends Resolver Consideration (`src/config/extends.rs`)

The extends resolver fetches remote configs and parses them with `serde_yaml::from_str`. Remote configs via `extends:` should remain YAML-only initially (or auto-detect based on the URL extension). This is an acceptable simplification for a first iteration because:

The `marked_yaml` crate is only referenced in `src/cli/commands/lint.rs` (as a mention in the `CLAUDE.md` notes) and is actually listed as a dependency but used only for source-location tracking in the lint system. Design an implementation plan for adding TOML configuration support to Bivvy, so users can use `bivvy.toml` (or `config.toml`) instead of `config.yml`.

## Current Architecture

The config loading system lives in `src/config/loader.rs`. Here's the key flow:

### File Discovery (`ConfigPaths::discover`)
Currently looks for hardcoded YAML file names:
- `~/.bivvy/config.yml` (user global)
- `.bivvy/config.yml` (project config - required)
- `.bivvy/config.local.yml` (local overrides)

### Loading Pipeline
1. `ConfigPaths::discover(project_root)` finds config files
2. For each file, `load_config_value(path)` reads it and parses as `serde_yaml::Value`
3. `merge_configs(&configs)` deep-merges all values (operates on `serde_yaml::Value`)
4. `serde_yaml::from_value(merged)` converts to `BivvyConfig`

### Key Functions
- `load_config_file(path)` → reads file, calls `parse_config(content, path)`
- `parse_config(content, path)` → `serde_yaml::from_str(content)` → `BivvyConfig`
- `load_config_value(path)` → `serde_yaml::from_str(&content)` → `serde_yaml::Value`
- `load_merged_config(project_root)` → discovers, loads as Values, merges, parses

### Merger
`src/config/merger.rs` operates entirely on `serde_yaml::Value` types. Deep merge algorithm handles objects recursively, replaces arrays, null deletes keys, etc.

### Schema
`src/config/schema.rs` - `BivvyConfig` and all nested types use `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]` from serde - they're format-agnostic.

### Error types
`BivvyError::ConfigParseError { path, message }` - already generic enough for any format.

## Implementation Plan: TOML Configuration Support for Bivvy

### 1. Overall Strategy: Option A -- Convert TOML to `serde_yaml::Value`

After examining the entire config pipeline, **Option A** is the right choice. Here is the rationale:

- The merger (`src/config/merger.rs`) operates entirely on `serde_yaml::Value`. Changing it to `serde_json::Value` (Option B) would require modifying the merger, the extends resolver, and every call site -- a large, risky refactor touching 5+ files.
- Option C (struct-level merging) loses critical merge semantics like "null deletes key."
- Option A requires adding a single conversion function (`toml::Value` to `serde_yaml::Value`) and adjusting file discovery. The merger, extends resolver, and all downstream consumers remain untouched.

The `toml::Value` to `serde_yaml::Value` conversion is straightforward because both are recursive enum types mapping to the same JSON-like data model: strings, integers, floats, booleans, arrays, and tables/mappings. The one edge case is that TOML distinguishes between `Integer` and `Float` while `serde_yaml::Value` uses `Number`, but both map naturally.

### 2. New Dependency

Add to `Cargo.toml` under `[dependencies]`:

```toml
toml = "0.8"
```

The `toml` crate version 0.8 is the current stable release. It provides `toml::Value` and `toml::from_str` for parsing.

### 3. Configuration Format Enum

Create a new enum in `src/config/loader.rs` to represent the detected format:

```rust
/// Configuration file format.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ConfigFormat {
    Yaml,
    Toml,
}
```

This will be stored in `ConfigPaths` so that all downstream code knows which format the project uses without re-detecting.

### 4. File Discovery Changes (`src/config/loader.rs`)

#### 4a. `ConfigPaths` struct modification

Add a `format` field:

```rust
pub struct ConfigPaths {
    pub extends: Vec<PathBuf>,
    pub user_global: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub project: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub project_local: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// The detected config format for this project.
    pub format: ConfigFormat,
}
```

#### 4b. Discovery logic

Each of the three `find_*` methods needs to check for both extensions. The file priority within a single location should be:

1. YAML first (`.yml`), since it is the existing default
2. TOML second (`.toml`)

But the critical constraint is: **all files in the merge chain must use the same format**. The discovery algorithm:

1. `find_project_config(project_root)` -- check for `.bivvy/config.yml` first, then `.bivvy/config.toml`. Whichever exists determines the project format. If both exist, return an error (see 4c).
2. Once the project format is known, `find_user_global()` looks for `~/.bivvy/config.yml` or `~/.bivvy/config.toml` based on the detected format.
3. `find_project_local(project_root)` looks for `.bivvy/config.local.yml` or `.bivvy/config.local.toml` based on the detected format.

The updated `discover` method becomes:

```rust
impl ConfigPaths {
    pub fn discover(project_root: &Path) -> std::result::Result<Self, BivvyError> {
        let (project, format) = Self::find_project_config(project_root)?;
        Ok(Self {
            extends: Vec::new(),
            user_global: Self::find_user_global(format),
            project,
            project_local: Self::find_project_local(project_root, format),
            format,
        })
    }
}
```

Note: `discover` currently returns `Self` (infallible). It must now return `Result<Self, BivvyError>` because it can fail if both formats exist. This is a breaking signature change. All callers of `ConfigPaths::discover()` must handle the Result.

#### 4c. Conflict detection

If both `.bivvy/config.yml` and `.bivvy/config.toml` exist, return a new error variant:

```rust
BivvyError::ConfigFormatConflict {
    path: PathBuf,  // the .bivvy directory
    message: String, // "Both config.yml and config.toml exist. Remove one."
}
```

This is added to `src/error.rs`.

#### 4d. Extension helper

Add a helper to get the file extension for a format:

```rust
impl ConfigFormat {
    pub fn extension(&self) -> &str {
        match self {
            ConfigFormat::Yaml => "yml",
            ConfigFormat::Toml => "toml",
        }
    }
    
    pub fn local_filename(&self) -> &str {
        match self {
            ConfigFormat::Yaml => "config.local.yml",
            ConfigFormat::Toml => "config.local.toml",
        }
    }
    
    pub fn config_filename(&self) -> &str {
        match self {
            ConfigFormat::Yaml => "config.yml",
            ConfigFormat::Toml => "config.toml",
        }
    }
}
```

### 5. TOML-to-YAML Value Conversion (`src/config/loader.rs`)

Add a conversion function:

```rust
/// Convert a toml::Value into serde_yaml::Value so it can be fed
/// into the existing merger pipeline unchanged.
fn toml_to_yaml_value(toml_val: &toml::Value) -> serde_yaml::Value {
    match toml_val {
        toml::Value::String(s) => serde_yaml::Value::String(s.clone()),
        toml::Value::Integer(i) => serde_yaml::Value::Number(serde_yaml::Number::from(*i)),
        toml::Value::Float(f) => {
            // serde_yaml::Number::from only takes i64/u64/f64
            serde_yaml::Value::Number(serde_yaml::Number::from(*f))
        }
        toml::Value::Boolean(b) => serde_yaml::Value::Bool(*b),
        toml::Value::Datetime(dt) => {
            // TOML datetimes have no direct YAML equivalent; store as string
            serde_yaml::Value::String(dt.to_string())
        }
        toml::Value::Array(arr) => {
            serde_yaml::Value::Sequence(arr.iter().map(toml_to_yaml_value).collect())
        }
        toml::Value::Table(table) => {
            let mut mapping = serde_yaml::Mapping::new();
            for (k, v) in table {
                mapping.insert(
                    serde_yaml::Value::String(k.clone()),
                    toml_to_yaml_value(v),
                );
            }
            serde_yaml::Value::Mapping(mapping)
        }
    }
}
```

This is about 25 lines of pure, easily-testable transformation code.

### 6. Loading Functions (`src/config/loader.rs`)

#### 6a. `load_config_value` -- format-aware

The current `load_config_value` always parses as YAML. It needs to accept a format parameter or detect format from the file extension:

```rust
/// Load a config file as raw serde_yaml::Value (for merging).
///
/// Detects format from the file extension (.toml vs .yml/.yaml).
pub fn load_config_value(path: &Path) -> Result<serde_yaml::Value> {
    let content = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| /* same as today */)?;
    
    let format = detect_format_from_path(path);
    match format {
        ConfigFormat::Toml => {
            let toml_val: toml::Value = toml::from_str(&content)
                .map_err(|e| BivvyError::ConfigParseError {
                    path: path.to_path_buf(),
                    message: e.to_string(),
                })?;
            Ok(toml_to_yaml_value(&toml_val))
        }
        ConfigFormat::Yaml => {
            serde_yaml::from_str(&content).map_err(|e| BivvyError::ConfigParseError {
                path: path.to_path_buf(),
                message: e.to_string(),
            })
        }
    }
}

fn detect_format_from_path(path: &Path) -> ConfigFormat {
    match path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) {
        Some("toml") => ConfigFormat::Toml,
        _ => ConfigFormat::Yaml,
    }
}
```

#### 6b. `parse_config` and `load_config_file` -- format-aware

Similarly, `parse_config` needs a TOML branch:

```rust
pub fn parse_config(content: &str, source_path: &Path) -> Result<BivvyConfig> {
    let format = detect_format_from_path(source_path);
    match format {
        ConfigFormat::Toml => {
            toml::from_str(content).map_err(|e| BivvyError::ConfigParseError {
                path: source_path.to_path_buf(),
                message: e.to_string(),
            })
        }
        ConfigFormat::Yaml => {
            serde_yaml::from_str(content).map_err(|e| BivvyError::ConfigParseError {
                path: source_path.to_path_buf(),
                message: e.to_string(),
            })
        }
    }
}
```

This works because `BivvyConfig` already derives `Serialize, Deserialize` from serde, which is format-agnostic. Both `toml::from_str` and `serde_yaml::from_str` use serde's deserialization framework.

When no project config is found, the error message currently hardcodes `config.yml`:

The `create_config` method in `InitCommand` currently generates YAML strings manually. For TOML, we need a parallel path. There are two approaches:

**Approach 1 (Recommended):** Keep the existing YAML string builder for YAML, and add a `create_config_toml` method that builds a TOML string. The TOML output would look like:

```toml

app_name = "MyApp"

[settings]
default_output = "verbose"  # verbose | quiet | silent

[steps.bundler]
template = "bundler"
# command = "bundle install"

[workflows.default]
```

I recommend Approach 1 because the init output is heavily commented and formatted for human readability -- this is not a purely mechanical serialization task.

```rust
    self.project_root.join(".bivvy/config.yml").exists()
```

1. **Accept the limitation**: TOML configs cannot use the "null deletes key" merge feature. This is acceptable because the feature is mainly used in `config.local.yml` overlays, and users choosing TOML can simply omit keys they don't want.

Users currently must write Bivvy config in YAML (`.bivvy/config.yml`). This adds TOML as an alternative format (`.bivvy/config.toml`), parsed with the `toml` crate. A project uses one format — no mixing.

**Convert TOML → `serde_yaml::Value`** so the existing merger pipeline is untouched. | `src/config/mod.rs` | Re-export `ConfigFormat` |
| `src/cli/args.rs` | Add `--format` flag to `InitArgs` |

| `src/cli/commands/lint.rs:86` | Handle `discover` returning `Result` |


**Add `ConfigFormat` enum:**
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]

    Yaml,
    Toml,
}
```

1. Check for `.bivvy/config.yml` and `.bivvy/config.toml`

- `src/config/loader.rs:213` (`load_merged_config_with_resolver`): add `?`
- `src/cli/commands/run.rs:188`: add `?` or `.unwrap_or_else` with graceful handling
- `src/cli/commands/lint.rs:86`: add `?`
- `src/cli/commands/config.rs:58`: add `?`

### 5. Update `load_merged_config` error message

When no project config found, reference both formats: "config.yml or config.toml".

- Add `--format` flag to `InitArgs` (values: `yaml`, `toml`; default: `yaml`)

Add `ConfigFormat` to the `loader` re-exports.

TOML has no `null` type, so the "null deletes key" merge feature won't work in TOML overlays. This is acceptable — users can simply omit keys they don't want. Document this.

- `toml_to_yaml_value`: string, int, float, bool, datetime, array, table, nested
- `detect_format_from_path`: `.yml`, `.toml`, no extension
- `ConfigPaths::discover`: finds `.toml`, prefers `.yml` when only it exists, errors on both
- `load_config_value` with TOML content
- `parse_config` with TOML content
- `load_merged_config` with TOML project + TOML local override
- `load_config_file` with `.toml` path
- Init command: `--format toml` creates `config.toml`, `config_exists` detects both formats
- Integration test: full TOML config workflow (load → validate)
- Error test: `ConfigFormatConflict` displays correctly

## Verification

```
cargo test --all-features
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo fmt -- --check
cargo build --release
```
